findings.reason: the unmeasured clause is the one the observed failure was made of, so the node can close on a refusal that repeats the diagnostic gap §17 records.
findings.text: §17's deliverable requires that a refused lane change leave the pointer untouched "and its result names why no worker started", but the gate's first case only requires that it "returns the refusal"; the incident itself was a command that printed `"ok": false` and named nothing, so a repair that keeps the pointer intact and still returns a bare failure returns exactly the uninformative result the section exists to replace and passes the gate

findings.reason: the gate covers two of the four named surfaces, and the run the section cites was refused by a read that was not `crew complete`.
findings.text: §23's deliverable names four surfaces ("`crew complete`, `crew observe` and the views") but its done-when exercises only the fold and `crew complete`, and the reads are not one fold: `reckon/crew/station_store.py` folds a stream through its own `_fold_stream` and `reckon/crew/recovery_stream.py` through `_observed_stream`, so a worker can correct the fold the two cases touch, leave a view or `crew observe` folding through the pointer's dialect, and still pass

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §17's gate does not measure the half of its deliverable that says the result names why no worker started, and §23's gate leaves two of the four surfaces its deliverable names unexercised.
